findings.title: Flow_config inputs drop template-only keys
findings.problem: buildFlowPackage sets `action.inputs = { ...inputs }`, replacing the template's Flow_config inputs wholesale and dropping threadKeyPrefix ('analytics-thread') and recentCount (10). The flow still reads both: Thread_key concats threadKeyPrefix and Recent_facts calls take(..., recentCount). flow-package.test.ts asserts toEqual(INPUTS), locking the behavior in.
findings.impact: Every imported flow builds thread keys as '-yyyy-MM' (may collide with unrelated cards) and passes null to take(), which is expected to fail the Teams scope on every delivery: a broken runtime path for the feature's core output (confirmed against definition.json).
findings.recommendation: Merge instead of replace: `action.inputs = { ...action.inputs, ...inputs }`, so threadKeyPrefix and recentCount survive; update the flow-package.test.ts expectation that currently locks in the wholesale replacement.
findings.check_notes: flow-package.ts:104 merges { ...action.inputs, ...inputs }; test asserts threadKeyPrefix/recentCount kept

findings.title: Stale webhook survives a re-walk of steps 1-4
findings.problem: Only resumeAt === 5 discards the saved webhookUrl/webhookTest. When reuse is declined (restart at 1) or resumeAt <= 4, the old values stay saved while the lead regenerates and re-imports a new flow; quitting before step 5 leaves a state the next run offers as reusable.

findings.recommendation: Discard webhookUrl/webhookTest whenever the run will re-execute step 4 (declined reuse or resumeAt <= 4), not only when resumeAt === 5, so a newly generated flow is never paired with the old trigger URL.

findings.title: Subsite folder links silently misparsed
findings.problem: parseFolderUrl's regex `^/(sites|teams)/([^/]+)/(.+?)` always takes the first two segments as the site, so a subsite folder (/sites/A/Sub/Shared Documents/X) parses as site /sites/A with folder 'Sub/Shared Documents/X' instead of being refused, although the doc-comment says subsites need separate entry.
findings.impact: The lead confirms a plausible-looking but wrong site/folder pair; the imported flow then targets a non-existent folder and deliveries fail.
findings.recommendation: Detect a folder path that does not start at a document library (e.g. the segment after /sites/<name>/ is not a library root such as "Shared Documents") and refuse with the "type manual" message, instead of folding the subsite into folderPath.
findings.check_notes: parseFolderUrl calls assertNotSubsite: view site path must match or folder must start at a default library

fix.change: parseFolderUrl rejects subsite folders with the 'type manual' message, using the library view's site path or the default library roots

findings.title: Guided path violates never-throws runner contract
findings.problem: runBootstrap returns runGuided(deps) unguarded; writeFlowPackage (cwd write), saveBootstrapState (mkdir/chmod), buildInstallCommand, inquirer prompt-close/Ctrl+C rejections, and non-validation errors rethrown by askValidated all propagate. The commander action in index.ts:109-110 has no catch.
findings.impact: Spec runner contract (exit code, never throws) is partially met: failures surface as raw stack traces with exitCode unset instead of a message and non-zero exit.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the guided call: `try { return await runGuided(deps); } catch (err) { deps.err(errorMessage(err)); return 1; }` (treat inquirer's prompt-close/ExitPromptError as a clean non-zero exit), so write/save/template/build errors become a message and exit code.
findings.check_notes: runBootstrap routes guided mode through runGuidedSafely: catch -> deps.err(message), return 1

fix.change: runBootstrap wraps runGuided in runGuidedSafely: a thrown error becomes a message on err and exit code 1
fix.test: run-bootstrap.test.ts > turns a guided-mode failure into a message and a non-zero exit instead of throwing

findings.title: Guided prompts write to stdout, breaking output split
findings.problem: createRealPrompter uses inquirer's default output stream (stdout), contradicting the spec/docs contract that only the install command goes to stdout. isTTY also requires process.stdout.isTTY, so `bootstrap > cmd.txt` is refused as 'No terminal is attached'.
findings.impact: The documented stdout/stderr split is unusable in guided mode: capturing the command mixes in prompt text, and redirecting stdout is rejected with a misleading message.
findings.recommendation: Create the inquirer prompts with `output: process.stderr` (e.g. via inquirer.createPromptModule({ output: process.stderr })) and base isTTY on stdin + stderr, so `bootstrap > cmd.txt` works and only the install command reaches stdout.
findings.check_notes: prompts via inquirer.createPromptModule({ output: process.stderr }); isTTY = stdin && stderr

fix.change: Real prompts use inquirer.createPromptModule({ output: process.stderr }); isTTY checks stdin and stderr

findings.title: Backslash passes the printable-value rule
findings.problem: FORBIDDEN_CHARACTERS is /["$`!]/; a backslash passes. Inside POSIX double quotes `\\` collapses to `\` and a trailing `\` escapes the closing quote, so the header's claim that the command is 'safe to pass to a shell as-is' does not hold for values containing `\`.
findings.impact: A webhook value with a backslash (e.g. hand-pasted URL with one in the query, which new URL() preserves) prints a command that passes a different value or breaks quoting.
findings.recommendation: Add `\` to FORBIDDEN_CHARACTERS (`/["$`!\\]/`) and the header/doc lists, so a double-quoted token can never collapse or escape its closing quote.
findings.check_notes: FORBIDDEN_CHARACTERS = /["$`!\\]/ now includes backslash; tests cover mid and trailing backslash

fix.change: Added backslash to FORBIDDEN_CHARACTERS and to the doc/error lists
fix.test: install-command.test.ts > webhook containing a backslash / a trailing backslash
